data.title: Parcel Carousel
data.statement:
A circular carousel carries parcels past a fixed collection arm. Compute the total number of one-slot movements needed to collect [[m]] parcels in a specified order.

<<Rules>>
- The carousel has [[n]] slots, initially containing one parcel each. Parcel IDs range from {{1}} to [[n]].
- The arm initially faces the first parcel listed in the input.
- Initially, parcels pass under the arm in input order: first, second, and so on, wrapping from the last slot to the first.
- The carousel moves in its current direction until the next requested parcel reaches the arm. That parcel is then collected.
- After every collection, the direction reverses, <<even if no movement was needed>>.
- A collected parcel leaves an empty slot. <<Empty slots remain on the carousel>> and count when moving.
- Moving by one slot counts as {{1}} movement. Collecting a parcel and reversing direction count as {{0}} movements.
- Each requested parcel is collected exactly once. Movement stops immediately after the final collection.

<<Example>>
With parcels {{1 2 3 4 5}} and collection order {{3 5 2}}:
- Reaching parcel {{3}} takes {{2}} movements.
- After reversing, reaching parcel {{5}} takes {{3}} movements.
- After reversing again, reaching parcel {{2}} takes {{2}} movements.

The total is {{7}} movements.
data.constraints:
{{1}} ≤ [[m]] ≤ [[n]] ≤ {{1000}}
{{1}} ≤ [[parcelId]] ≤ [[n]]
{{1}} ≤ [[requestedId]] ≤ [[n]]

All [[parcelId]] values are distinct.
All [[requestedId]] values are distinct.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

A circular carousel carries parcels past a fixed collection arm. Compute the total number of one-slot movements needed to collect m parcels in a specified order.

Rules
- The carousel has n slots, initially containing one parcel each. Parcel IDs range from 1 to n.
- The arm initially faces the first parcel listed in the input.
- Initially, parcels pass under the arm in input order: first, second, and so on, wrapping from the last slot to the first.
- The carousel moves in its current direction until the next requested parcel reaches the arm. That parcel is then collected.
- After every collection, the direction reverses, even if no movement was needed.
- A collected parcel leaves an empty slot. Empty slots remain on the carousel and count when moving.
- Moving by one slot counts as 1 movement. Collecting a parcel and reversing direction count as 0 movements.
- Each requested parcel is collected exactly once. Movement stops immediately after the final collection.

Example
With parcels 1 2 3 4 5 and collection order 3 5 2:
- Reaching parcel 3 takes 2 movements.
- After reversing, reaching parcel 5 takes 3 movements.
- After reversing again, reaching parcel 2 takes 2 movements.

The total is 7 movements.
Input
Line 1: Two space-separated integers n and m: the number of slots and the number of parcels to collect.

Line 2: n space-separated integers parcelId, describing the parcels in clockwise order around the carousel. Each ID from 1 to n appears exactly once. The arm initially faces the first listed parcel.

Line 3: m space-separated integers requestedId, describing the required collection order. All requested IDs are distinct.
Output
Line 1: A single integer: the total number of one-slot movements needed to collect all requested parcels in the specified order.
Constraints
1 ≤ m ≤ n ≤ 1000
1 ≤ parcelId ≤ n
1 ≤ requestedId ≤ n

All parcelId values are distinct.
All requestedId values are distinct.
Example
Input
5 3
1 2 3 4 5
3 5 2
Output
7
